arxiv-2012-01030.title: MAAD-Face: A Massively Annotated Attribute Dataset for Face Images
arxiv-2012-01030.creator: Philipp Terhörst, Daniel Fährmann, Jan Niklas Kolf, Naser Damer, Florian Kirchbuchner, and Arjan Kuijper
arxiv-2012-01030.description: Abstract Soft-biometrics play an important role in face biometrics and related fields since these might lead to biased performances, threaten the user’s privacy, or are valuable for commercial aspects. Current face databases are specifically constructed for the development of face recognition applications.

arxiv-2101-02395.title: Gluon Gravitational Form Factors at Large Momentum Transfer
arxiv-2101-02395.creator: Xuan-Bo Tong, Jian-Ping Ma, Feng Yuan
arxiv-2101-02395.description: Abstract We perform a perturbative QCD analysis of the gluonic gravitational form factors (GFFs) of the proton and pion at large momentum transfer. We derive the explicit factorization formula of the GFFs in terms of the distribution amplitudes of hadrons.

arxiv-2105-07565.title: Attention Elasticities and Invariant Information Costs Thanks: I thank Andrew Caplin for helpful comments and discussions.
arxiv-2105-07565.creator: Dániel Csaba
arxiv-2105-07565.description: Abstract We consider a generalization of rational inattention problems by measuring costs of information through the information radius ( Sibson 1969 ; Verdú 2015 ) of statistical experiments. We introduce a notion of attention elasticity measuring the sensitivity of attention strategies with respect to changes in incentives.

arxiv-2108-02857.title: Asymptotics of Yule’s nonsense correlation for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths: a Wiener chaos approach.
arxiv-2108-02857.creator: Soukaina Douissi, Frederi Viens, Khalifa Es-Sebaiy
arxiv-2108-02857.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the distribution of the so-called "Yule’s nonsense correlation statistic" on a time interval [ 0 , T ] [0,T] for a time horizon T > 0 T>0 , when T T is large, for a pair ( X 1 , X 2 ) (X_{1},X_{2}) of independent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.

The Pristine survey – XXII. A serendipitous discovery of an extremely Li-rich very meta
arxiv-2310-07907.creator: T. M. Sitnova, T. Matsuno, Z. Yuan, N. F. Martin, P. Banerjee, F. Sestito, K. A. Venn, J. I. González Hernández
arxiv-2310-07907.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by T. M. Sitnova, T. Matsuno, Z. Yuan, N. F. Martin, P. Banerjee, F. Sestito, K. A. Venn, J. I. González Hernández. arxiv-2408-09831.title: Ranking Generated Answers
arxiv-2408-09831.creator: Sebastian Heineking, Jonas Probst, Daniel Steinbach, Martin Potthast, Harrisen Scells
arxiv-2408-09831.description: Abstract Evaluating the output of generative large language models (LLMs) is challenging and difficult to scale. Many evaluations of LLMs focus on tasks such as single-choice question-answering or text classification. These tasks are not suitable for assessing open-ended question-answering capabilities, which are critical in domains where expertise is required.

arxiv-2412-00158.title: Auger Open Data and the Pierre Auger Observatory International Masterclasses
arxiv-2412-00158.creator: E Santos 1, for the Pierre Auger Collaboration 2
arxiv-2412-00158.description: Abstract The Pierre Auger Observatory has a public data policy following the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable). We aim to share the data with the scientific community as part of the multi-messenger effort at different levels and for educational activities to engage the general public. Following the first portal created in 2007, a new portal hosted at https://opendata.auger.

arxiv-2511-06132.title: On the Convergence and Stability of Distributed Sub-model Training
arxiv-2511-06132.creator: Yuyang Deng † Fuli Qiao ∗ Mehrdad Mahdavi ∗ † Columbia University ∗ The Pennsylvania State University yd282@columbia.edu {fvq5015,mzm616}@psu.edu
arxiv-2511-06132.description: Abstract As learning models continue to grow in size, enabling on-device local training of these models has emerged as a critical challenge in federated learning. A popular solution is sub-model training, where the server only distributes randomly sampled sub-models to the edge clients, and clients only update these small models.

arxiv-2511-21180.title: CAHS-Attack: CLIP-Aware Heuristic Search Attack Method for Stable Diffusion
arxiv-2511-21180.creator: Shuhan Xia, Jing Dai, Hui Ouyang, Yadong Shang, Dongxiao Zhao, Peipei Li
arxiv-2511-21180.description: Abstract Diffusion models exhibit notable fragility when faced with adversarial prompts, and strengthening attack capabilities is crucial for uncovering such vulnerabilities and building more robust generative systems. Existing works often rely on white-box access to model gradients or hand-crafted prompt engineering, which is infeasible in real-world deployments due to restricted access or poor attack effect.

arxiv-2512-08379.title: DeepFeature: Iterative Context-aware Feature Generation for Wearable Biosignals Thanks: † These authors contributed equally to this work.
arxiv-2512-08379.creator: Kaiwei Liu 1,† , Yuting He 1,† , Bufang Yang 1 , Mu Yuan 1 , Chun Man Victor Wong 2 , Ho Pong Andrew Sze 3 , Zhenyu Yan 1 , Hongkai Chen 1
arxiv-2512-08379.description: Abstract . Biosignals collected from wearable devices are widely utilized in healthcare applications. Machine learning models used in these applications often rely on features extracted from biosignals due to their effectiveness, lower data dimensionality, and wide compatibility across various model architectures.

pmc-10544112.title: Clinical research stakeholders’ experiences of clinical research during COVID-19: a qualitative study
pmc-10544112.creator: Christine FitzGerald, Aoife Vaughan-Witts, Louise Barry, Gillian Corey, Fiona Leahy, Siobhán Egan, Elaine Conway, Margaret O’Connor, Rose Galvin
pmc-10544112.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic created a complex high-risk clinical research environment with clinical research activities significantly impacted. Clinical research stakeholders adapted rapidly to new clinical practices; PPE, infection control policies, all while engaging with a more unwell patient demographic. The aim of this study is to explore the experiences of conducting clinical research during COVID-19 with clinical research stakeholders.

pmc-11495721.title: Acute myeloid leukemia with NPM1, IDH2, and SETD2 mutations mimicking acute promyelocytic leukemia: A case report and literature review
pmc-11495721.creator: Xiang-Lei Chen, Shan-Shan Zeng
pmc-11495721.description: Rationale:Acute myeloid leukemia with NPM1, IDH2, and SETD2 mutations can mimic acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) and poses a challenge for the early and accurate differentiation and diagnosis of APL with PML::RARA.Patient concerns:A 70-year-old man was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia with NPM1, IDH2, and SETD2 mutations.Diagnosis:APL-like acute myeloid leukemia with NPM1, IDH2, and SETD2 mutations was made.

pmc-12374928.title: The transcription factor FOXA1 upregulates PYCR1-mediated autophagy to suppress antitumor immunity in lung adenocarcinoma
pmc-12374928.creator: Kui Liu, Xiaoyan Yang, Xuemei Tang, Bo Tang
pmc-12374928.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundImmunotherapy has emerged as an effective treatment for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) in recent years. However, the ability of cancer cells to suppress antitumor immune responses through multiple mechanisms has become one of the major challenges for therapy.

pmc-12469273.title: The Novel Flax Cultivar Silesia Shows High Morphogenetic Capacity in Tissue Cultures
pmc-12469273.creator: Mateusz Lipiński, Kinga Pilarska-Dudziak, Tadeusz Czuj, Anna Prescha, Wojciech Łaba, Katarzyna Skórkowska-Telichowska, Magdalena Wróbel-Kwiatkowska
pmc-12469273.description: The aim of the present study was to evaluate the morphogenetic efficiency of the new flax (Linum usitatissimum L.) cultivar Silesia. The plant material consisted of five ecotypes of Silesia seeds selected by determining the fatty acid composition in individual plants.

pmc-12771754.title: Unveiling the ITGβ1-CLIC1 axis: a new frontier in oral squamous cell carcinoma progression and immune evasion: insights from the tumor-mimetic ECM system
pmc-12771754.creator: Yungang He, Renjie Shuai, Jian Wu, Lian Zhou
pmc-12771754.description: BackgroundThe progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is critically influenced by the dynamic interaction between the tumor and immunosuppressive microenvironment. Integrin β1 (ITGβ1, ITGB1), a pivotal mediator of cell-extracellular matrix (ECM) interaction, not only facilitates tumor invasion but may also plays a role in immune evasion, which remains inadequately understood.

pmc-12799947.title: TMEtyper: A computational method for tumor microenvironment subtyping with applications in immunotherapy
pmc-12799947.creator: Yaru Miao, Tong Zhou, Yan Li, Jie Yao, Yanghui Bi, Ruiping Zhang
pmc-12799947.description: BackgroundThe heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment (TME) is a critical determinant of outcomes in immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy. However, robust methodological frameworks for systematically characterizing this heterogeneity and identifying causal regulators of treatment response are still lacking.MethodsWe developed TMEtyper, a comprehensive computational framework for TME characterization.

pmc-13213015.title: Severe Phototoxic Vesiculobullous Eruption Following Sequential Exposure to Terbinafine, Ciprofloxacin, and Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole
pmc-13213015.creator: Roberto R Gonzalez Alvarez
pmc-13213015.description: Phototoxic drug eruptions are well-recognized adverse reactions to several classes of medications, including fluoroquinolones, sulfonamides, and antifungals. However, sequential photosensitization following exposure to multiple agents is rarely described. We present the case of a 44-year-old Hispanic male commercial driver who developed a severe, vesiculobullous, photo-distributed rash following sequential exposure to terbinafine, ciprofloxacin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim).

pmc-13243586.title: Mode of action guided metagenomic natural product discovery reveals convergent evolution of a ClpP-targeting motif
pmc-13243586.creator: Jingbo Kan, Kaylyn Spotton, Adrian Morales-Amador, Yozen Hernandez, Ján Burian, Cecilia Panfil, Melinda A. Ternei, Robert E. Boer, Abir Bhattacharjee, Sean F. Brady
pmc-13243586.description: The discovery of natural products with specific modes of action from metagenomes remains challenging. Here, we present resistance-CONKAT-seq, a pipeline that links biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) to self-resistance genes, enabling identification of metabolites with desired molecular targets. Using clpP-directed resistance-CONKAT-seq, we identify the calprotamides, which activate native ClpP and enhance its activity.

pmc-13246303.title: Spatiotemporal deep learning for scar screening in cardiovascular magnetic resonance: Toward selective use of gadolinium
pmc-13246303.creator: Amine Amyar, Shiro Nakamori, Jiwon Kim, Martin S Maron, Ethan J Rowin, Karishma Pareek, Alexander Schulz, Robert M Judd, Warren J Manning, Raymond Y Kwong, Frederick L Ruberg, Jonathan W Weinsaft, Reza Nezafat

pmc-13530299.title: Ubiquitination-driven proteostasis remodeling underlies oxidative stress and actin degradation in citrus huanglongbing
pmc-13530299.creator: Min Li, Hongkun Qin, Yundan Hu, Bingqian Qin, Zirui Fan, Mingzhuo Li, Yaping Mao, Fajin Liao, Zhigang Ouyang, Huan Chen, Shuo Duan
pmc-13530299.description: Citrus huanglongbing, caused by Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (CLas), is associated with severe metabolic disruption, chronic immune activation, and progressive decline of citrus trees, but the posttranslational mechanisms underlying these responses remain poorly understood. Here, we combined ubiquitinated peptide immunoaffinity enrichment with 4D label-free quantitative proteomics to profile protein abundance and protein ubiquitination in infected sweet orange leaves.

pmc-13572082.title: Designing eligibility and evaluation criteria for antibacterial pull incentives: a comparative review of implemented and emerging initiatives
pmc-13572082.creator: Michael Anderson, Emily O'Neill, Gunnar Ljungqvist, Avi Cherla, Zilke Claessens, Elise Schoefs, Nick Crabb, Warren Cowell, Jennifer Cohn, Deepali Patel, Elias Mossialos
pmc-13572082.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryBackgroundPull incentives aim to improve the commercial viability of antibacterials, but the criteria determining which products and companies qualify have not been compared across countries. We compared product and company eligibility and evaluation criteria across these incentives.MethodsWe conducted an umbrella review of MEDLINE and Embase for English-language reviews of pull incentives targeting antibacterial innovation and access (2014 to 14 October 2024), supplemented by grey literature searches and the Global AMR R&D Hub dashboard (December 2025).
